On site · 1:1

Massing, both options

Align once against two known points. Then swap between the two options without leaving AR — they share an origin and a bounding box, so the comparison is honest and the alignment is kept.

On site, in order

  1. Align. Point 1 = SE corner, point 2 = spur meets lot — 43 m apart, the longest baseline you have. Scrape the grass back before setting each one.

  2. Check the baseline number. Under a metre is good. Past 1.5 m it warns you; re-align rather than trusting the view.

  3. Re-pin, don't re-align. Moved to the far end and the model has drifted? Stand on any known point and tap Re-pin here. One point, heading kept, five seconds.

  4. Swap options from the chips at the top of the panel. Alignment survives.

Blue ring = a surface the phone is confident about. No ring means you're aiming at sky, at something unmapped, or it has lost tracking. Don't set a point without it.

Metric, 1:1, +Y north · levels are local RL, not a survey datum
Ground off a LiDAR surface, ±0.2 m — good for design, not for setting out
Needs Chrome on Android with Google Play Services for AR, over https.
